title: South Korean student facing cheating claim found ‘in state of cardiac arrest’
html:
Lee Jin-woo shot to fame after scoring perfect marks on the law school admission test while studying dentistry at the prestigious Seoul National University.

PHOTO: EPA

AI generated

SEOUL – A South Korean man whose perfect score on a law school admission test raised suspicions of artificial intelligence-assisted cheating was found “in a state of cardiac arrest” on Nov 19 following suicide concerns, the South Korean police said.

Lee Jin-woo shot to fame in 2026 after scoring perfect marks on the law school admission test while studying dentistry at the prestigious Seoul National University.

But since Nov 15, when the top scorer in the 2026 national tax accountant exam confessed to cheating using AI, suspicions have swirled around the 32-year-old, who denied the allegations.

In an attempt to refute the claims, he pledged to demonstrate his abilities by live-streaming himself taking the Korean language section of the college entrance exam on Nov 19, but failed to show up.

Lee “was found in a state of cardiac arrest at an undisclosed location in Gangdong district”, the police said in a brief statement, referencing “a report filed today over suicide concerns involving a man in his 30s”.

The South Korean authorities often take time to pronounce people as dead, categorising the lifeless as being “in a state of cardiac arrest”.

“If he is pronounced dead, the authorities will conduct a forensic examination and other procedures to determine the circumstances,” the police statement added.

Questions have also emerged over his college entrance exam scores, which rose sharply from his results in the 2010s and secured him a place at SNU’s dental school.

The local media has also reported allegations of past assault and extortion unrelated to the AI cheating claims. AFP
